cause_quote: The new `await executeSharedSessionCronJob(` branch sent existing named-session jobs through a handoff that fell back to `\`Session event execution ${outcome}\`` whenever terminal evidence had no error text, even when the reply operation held the exception.
user_saw: Operators saw only “Session event execution failed” in run history and the job’s last error, with no explanation of what went wrong.
summary: The fix records the reply operation’s failure cause when terminal evidence has no error detail and uses the generic message only if no cause is available.
reasoning: I checked the causing commit’s parent and confirmed that named-session jobs went through the isolated runner, whose catch normalized the thrown exception into the error the cron service returned. The refactor routed those same jobs through session-event settlement, which published the fallback when the error handler had stored the cause on the reply operation without supplying usable terminal error text. The later settlement extraction preserved that fallback, and the stopped-turn fix used the operation cause for classification while leaving the recorded error unchanged.
